summary: Amplified health-check + ephemeral key rotation fanout causing sustained 429s for bulk ingest
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-05 03:10 UTC Acme Analytics observed a rapid increase in 429 responses across their bulk-ingest jobs. The errors correlate with scheduled ephemeral API key rotation and concurrent health-check sweeps from their orchestrator. Impact: ~40% of chunked uploads were rejected with 429s over a 45-minute window; ingestion lag increased and downstream retry waves amplified tenant token exhaustion. Environment: Dedicated pool (reserved), prod-us-west, tenant id T-ACME-77. Customer reports they did not change upload concurrency during the window. They are blocked from completing nightly backfills.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a bulk upload orchestrator with 200 parallel workers pointing at the dedicated pool route
2) Enable ephemeral key rotation every 5 minutes (short-lived credentials) and immediate re-registration of worker sessions
3) Ensure the orchestrator has health-check probes configured to ping the /ready endpoint every 10s across all workers
4) Trigger a large split upload (250GB split into ~5000 chunks) and observe rate-limiter metrics and 429 counts
logs: 2026-03-05T03:10:13Z tenant=T-ACME-77 worker=orchestrator-12 event=session_reconnect route=/v1/embeds status=429 quota_remain=0
comments: Ava Chen (2026-03-05): Customer reached out via support form at 03:15 UTC reporting elevated 429s during their nightly ingest. Provided initial logs and sample request IDs. Asked for immediate mitigation advice.

Diego Martinez (Support, 2026-03-05): Acknowledged; opened ticket and requested tenant-level rate-limiter dump and exact key-rotation schedule. Added priority P1 due to ingestion blocking. Suggested temporary reduce of concurrency if possible.

Priya Nair (SRE, 2026-03-05): Pulled rate-limiter traces. Observed synchronized drain of tenant token bucket coincident with ephemeral key rebinds and a wave of health-check retries. Hypothesis: key rotation forced clients to re-auth and re-open connections; combined with aggressive health probes this produced a short-lived fanout that consumed burst credits across many routes.

Customer (Acme Support, 2026-03-05): Confirmed orchestrator rotates keys every 5 minutes and health checks are across all workers. Asked for configuration recommendations to avoid losing burst credits.

Diego Martinez (Support, 2026-03-06): Applied a temporary tenant-level burst increase on dedicated pool (x2 for 30 minutes) to allow backlog flush. Customer confirmed immediate drop in 429s but noted concern about recurrence during next rotation window.

Priya Nair (SRE, 2026-03-07): Requested follow-up with engineering to consider non-blocking rebind behavior for ephemeral keys and to add exemption for internal health probes from tenant token accounting (or route health-checks to internal admin route).

Diego Martinez (Support, 2026-03-09): Sent recommended long-term configuration and steps to customer; waiting for them to apply staggered rotation and probe changes. Marked ticket In Progress while monitoring next scheduled rotation.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 03:10:12 rotate_keys -> 03:10:13 immediate reconnects -> 03:10:15 token bucket drained -> 03:10:17 first retry wave

Metric correlation: tenant_token_bucket shows negative burst balance starting 03:10:15 for ~45 minutes. edge-proxy logs show simultaneous TCP reconnects from ~180 workers leading to duplicate preflight/accounting for short window.
Hypothesis A: Ephemeral key rotation triggers worker re-registration calls that are counted against tenant quota and are not deduped during short windows, amplifying short-lived fanout.
Hypothesis B: Health-check probes are treated as regular requests on the same route and consume burst credits; combined with rebind traffic they push the tenant over the refill threshold.

Reproduction: Dev ran a simulated rotation+probe burst in staging with 120 simulated workers and reproduced 429 spike when rotation + probes overlapped. Verified mitigation by either staggering rotation or routing health-checks to admin path that uses internal exemption pool.
Cross-reference: Related to SUP-712999 (control-plane mirror private vpc opaque 429s) for cases where control-plane traffic is counted against tenant; see runbook link below.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation applied: increased tenant burst allowance on dedicated pool for 30 minutes and advised customer to pause bulk uploads for next rotation window. Immediate effect: 429s dropped to <2% of baseline.
- Stagger ephemeral key rotation across worker sets (e.g., rotate subsets every 5m so not all workers rebind simultaneously).
- Reconfigure health-checks to hit a separate admin-ready route (/internal/ready) that is mapped to an internal exemption pool or has a different burst budget.
- If using very short-lived credentials (<10m), increase rotation granularity or use session refresh that does not force new connection creation at the same time across workers.

- Engineering to investigate deduplication window for re-registration calls during key rotation and consider an adaptive debounce to avoid immediate token accounting spikes. (ENG-issue link provided).
- Add documentation section for 'ephemeral key rotation patterns' and recommended probe routing; link drafted to Confluence runbook.
- Consider adding a configuration option in Dedicated Console: 'Exclude probe routes from tenant burst accounting' as a configurator for enterprise/dedicated customers.
Ticket state: Waiting on customer to apply staggered rotation and probe route changes; Support to monitor next rotation (2026-03-12 scheduled) and will close if no repeat.
